title: The Children's Book Job (S38E01)
text: "The Children's Book Job" is the Season 38 premiere (the 810th episode overall, production code 37ABF10), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing September 27, 2026. When Springfield Elementary faces closure over low test scores and owl infestations, Marge rallies the PTA and Principal Largo suggests recruiting reclusive children's author Constance Clavinger, creator of The Plucky Little Goat, to save the day. Homer is sent to pick her up and finds her drunk at The Pilot's Room, and a boutique shoplifting arrest soon sends the two on the run, with Snake stealing Homer's car (and the book) along the way. After a chase, a concussed Homer hallucinates a children's-book fantasy, and at the fair Constance tells a story about her day with Homer; the two end up with matching goat and hippo tattoos. Guest starring Emma Thompson as Constance Clavinger and Colin Jost as himself.

title: Diary of a Chimpy Kid (S38E02)
text: "Diary of a Chimpy Kid" is an episode of Season 38 (the 811th episode overall, production code 37ABF09), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing October 4, 2026. After Itchy & Scratchy enters the public domain and becomes Krusty Babies!, Krusty fires the babies and a chimp. Bart and Lisa adopt the chimp, naming him Mr. Goodboy, and clash over parenting styles: Bart is overprotective while Lisa follows a free-range parenting book. Homer fears the chimp will tear off his face, and school counseling follows. Bart's tracker leads them to Freedom Chimps, a libertarian private zoo and shooting range, where Lisa tosses the keys and frees the monkeys; the zoo is shut down for 30 violations, and the kids finally let Mr. Goodboy go. Guest starring Ike Barinholtz as Wayne the Grip.

title: Comic Book Guy
text: Comic Book Guy, whose real name is Jeffrey "Jeff" Albertson, is the owner of The Android's Dungeon comic book store in Springfield, a recurring minor character. Comic Book Guy is an obese, unkempt, and socially awkward comic shop owner whose sharp sarcasm masks a lifetime of loneliness and insecurity. Despite holding a master's degree in folklore and mythology, he channels his intelligence into obsessive devotion to comics, sci-fi, and pop culture trivia, often looking down on customers like Bart and Milhouse from behind his counter. His childhood was shaped by an emotionally distant, wealthy father who struggled to connect with him, leaving him with lingering insecurities into adulthood. Romantically, he spent decades as a virgin before eventually dating Edna Krabappel and Agnes Skinner, and finally finding lasting love with Kumiko, whom he marries and later considers starting a family with. He briefly finds mainstream success as the creator of the comic series Everyman, even seeing it adapted into a troubled Hollywood film starring Homer Simpson. Known for his biting insults and superiority complex, he's most famous for his recurring put-down about things being the 'worst ever,' a signature line that defines his cynical persona. Voiced by Hank Azaria.
